input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 is a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly stripped of any reduction or termination right — squarely in our walk-away territory and well short of the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, shortfall handled by true-up). It also contradicts § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer "has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment") and undercuts our § 9.4 convenience-termination right. No other clause supplies a reduction, exit, or true-up mechanic: § 7.1 only fixes Fees per Order Form and the § 22.2-22.3 shortfall language relates to usage audits, not to this commitment. We therefore redline § 2.1 to the fallback with a single surgical replacement, leaving the rest of the payment architecture intact.

proposal.summary: Narrow § 2.1 take-or-pay to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up instead of a penalty.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights, which also conflicts with the no-minimum-volume acknowledgement in § 12.3 and our convenience-termination right in § 9.4. Our fallback limits the commitment to the current 12-month term, allows reduction on 30 days' notice, and settles any shortfall by true-up rather than penalty.

ops.newText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services during the current twelve-month term only. Customer may reduce that commitment on thirty days' notice, and any shortfall is settled by a true-up rather than a penalty.
